title: Distances and isoperimetric inequalities in random triangulations of high genus
summary: Equation (12) uses an incorrect exponential base in Lemma 14. Equation (16) is overgeneralized to same-tentacle edges. Neither result establishes a false final theorem.

problems.title: Incorrect exponential base in Lemma 14
problems.source_locator: PDF/printed page 18, Lemma 14, equation (12), with definitions on pp.16-18
assumptions: T_n=a n, M_n=2 b n; positive a,b bounded away from zero on Lemma13 event
ell odd, ell tends to infinity with ell=o(n), including ell=s log n+O(1)
word has ell-1 up steps and 2ell-1 down steps
problems.evidence_method: analytic proof and independent exact-rational arithmetic
problems.decisive_check: u_ell/q^(3ell)=(pq)^(-1)(p/q)^ell ->0; -log(1-u_ell)~u_ell; hence normalized negative logarithm of LHS tends to0 and cannot exceed a fixed positive c'. Uniformly on count event p/q<=1/2 and p is bounded below, so random variation in a,b does not rescue it.
counterevidence: Source page image confirms c=q; not OCR reversal
Changing c to the smaller step probability p gives a valid repair
Theorem only needs an unspecified sufficiently small positive s, not the printed larger admissible range
core_dependency: Theorem4 upper Cheeger bound uses Lemma14 on p18
Proposition17 height lower bound uses Lemma14 on p20
problems.impact: Invalid central derivation, not a false final theorem. Earlier isoperimetry/diameter proofs do not rely on (12).

correction.statement: With a>=a0>0,b>=b0>0,a<=3,b<=1, choose p0=min(b0/6,1/2), kappa=(a0+3b0)/6. Failure <= exp(-kappa n p0^(3ell)/ell); choose s<1/(3log(1/p0)).
correction.verification: Proved uniform probability estimate, and conditioning on probability Omega(n^-1/2) preserves convergence. Encoding/count/conditioning inputs are retained assumptions, not independently re-proved external literature.

problems.title: Distance decomposition requires distinct tentacles
problems.source_locator: PDF/printed p20 equation(16); exceptional-event restriction p21
problems.claim: For any two oriented edges, distance=H(e1)+H(e2)+core distance+epsilon with epsilon in [-2,2]
assumptions: Ladders inserted using the definition on p16
Two oriented edges inside the same deep tentacle are allowed by the printed unrestricted quantifier
For e1=e2, H(e)>1; alternatively two distinct outgoing edges at a deep common starting vertex
problems.decisive_check: For e1=e2 both distances are0, requiring epsilon=-2H(e)<-2. A fixed finite deep ladder may be inserted into a genus-g_n core with 2(n-k) faces when n-k>=2g_n-1, which holds eventually for theta<1/2. This yields an admissible triangulation with2n faces and unchanged genus.
counterevidence: Page21 explicitly discards shared-tentacle pairs before the final exchangeability argument
Different tentacles force exit through base endpoints; the decomposition has the intended restricted use
problems.core_dependency: Proposition17 uses a restriction later that removes this counterexample; no extra central harm demonstrated

correction.statement: Restrict equation(16) to distinct tentacles and impose the already-used exceptional-event restriction before applying it
correction.verification: Domain repair supported; not independent re-proof of Proposition17
